newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - SE Asian hit by weak demand, ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - SE Asian hit by weak demand, ample supply.

text.p: The Southeast Asian rubber market is in for another dreary week as soft demand and ample supplies are seen keeping prices on the defensive, regional traders said on Monday.
Rising stocks in Japan and the absence of China from the market will make an already bearish situation worse, they said.
"The market's virtually dead, with very little or no interest at all shown by American and European buyers," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.
"The fundamental picture looks so bad. The Thais are selling, production is up with wintering now over, and Japan's stock position is high. It's not encouraging," a dealer in Singapore added.
Dealers said consumers are staying out on the belief that prices will soften further.

"The only thing that will lift the market is offtake. But buyers are staying on the sidelines because they think prices are going to come off some more," a dealer for a Japanese trading house in Singapore said.
One trader in Thailand, the world's biggest producer of natural rubber, said "prices now are lower than those two years ago. Market ideas seem to be that prices will drop further."
The Thai benchmark RSS3 grade rubber for June delivery was quoted around 110.00-112.00 U.S. cents a kg FOB Bangkok against 116.00 cents last week.
One trader in Thailand said shortcovering should shore up the price of RSS3. "I think buyers will have to raise the bidding prices otherwise no one will sell to them," he said.
The market will also try to shake off the effects of the Eid Al-Adha holiday Moslem holiday last Friday and the Songkran Buddhist New Year holidays in Thailand earlier last week.
In Indonesia, traders said the benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 rubber will probably fall this week amid thin buying interest.
"I think prices will continue to fall because demand is very low," said one trader.
"We just assume that buyers are well-stocked as they are not doing much purchasing," another Indonesian-based dealer said.
A deal was done last Thursday at 47.75 U.S. cents a lb in Banjarmasin for July shipment, but most traders in other cities were reluctant to sell at such low prices.

Traders in Surabaya quoted their offer prices at 48.00 cents a lb for June shipment. They said SIR20 was unchanged at 48.50 cents a lb FOB Medan, at 48.25 cents FOB Palembang, at 48.00 cents FOB Padang and at 47.75 cents FOB Pontianak and Jambi.
Malaysian traders said they expect the market to drift lower this week, due mainly to the absence of any indicators showing the return of consumer demand.
"I think it's very likely that prices will fall by a half cent to one cent every day this week," a trader said. "That would mean 2.5-5.0 (Malaysian) cents down for the whole week."
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 at the close of the market last week at 287.50 cents a kg and the SMR20 at 270.50 cents a kg, both for May buyer.
Trading houses offered SMR 20 at 271 cents, SMR CV at 342 cents, SMR L at 322 cents, SMR 5 at 282 cents, SMR 10 at 272 cents and drum latex at 231 cents.
Traders said there were no sales except for some small parcels of latex and SMR20 grade rubber.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
